europe_now.title: Crimea Bridge partially collapses after explosions
europe_now.summary: Video footage shows a section of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to annexed Crimea collapsing following explosions, disrupting a critical Russian supply route. Ukrainian officials have not claimed responsibility but have previously targeted the bridge as a legitimate military objective.

sources.headline: New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses
Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea

europe_now.title: Polish constitutional court lifts chief justice immunity
europe_now.summary: The country's contested constitutional tribunal has removed legal immunity from the Supreme Court's first president, allowing criminal proceedings against her to proceed. The ruling intensifies a years-long dispute over judicial independence and the rule of law in Poland.

sources.headline: Polish constitutional court strips chief justice of immunity to face criminal charges

top_stories.title: Ukraine conflict escalation
top_stories.summary: A key bridge connecting Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula suffered a partial collapse after explosions, with video evidence showing the moment of failure. Ukrainian forces have intensified attacks on the crossing, which serves as a vital logistics artery for Russian troops, while Moscow deploys new low-cost munitions to counter Kyiv's advances.

sources.headline: New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses
Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea

top_stories.title: EU policy and regulation
top_stories.summary: The European Court of Auditors has warned that existing regulations contain significant gaps that leave public health exposed to hazardous persistent chemicals. Meanwhile, the EU has adopted voluntary targets to secure supplies of critical raw materials for high-tech industries, and the Commission faces accusations of withholding correspondence related to a controversial patent law decision.

sources.headline: EU auditors say rules ‘full of holes’ leave health at risk from toxic forever chemicals
Commission accused of withholding emails on killing patent law

top_stories.title: French political landscape
top_stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe has outlined a platform of spending cuts and a higher retirement age as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race. The field of potential candidates continues to expand, adding uncertainty to the succession of President Emmanuel Macron.

sources.headline: French ex-PM Philippe pledges to slash spending, hike retirement age as Elysée bid falters
French presidential elections 2027: More candidates, more confusion (Episode 2)

top_stories.title: China-EU-Ukraine dynamics
top_stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping sought to project neutrality on the Ukraine war during a summit in Shenzhen, even as EU observers warn that Beijing's support for Moscow risks damaging relations with Europe. The meeting coincided with a high-profile trilateral gathering involving the leaders of the United States, Russia, and China, highlighting competing diplomatic agendas.

sources.headline: Xi keen to look ‘neutral’ on Ukraine at Shenzhen summit, as China risks spoling EU relations by helping Putin to wage war
